scientific_purpose: control condition; reference for all other conditions
empirical_basis: this trial IS the measured baseline (design doc section 2), not derived from it
expected_effect: none by construction (immediate passthrough, byte-identical to no relay)

scientific_purpose: isolate a moderate, steady, sub-peer_timeout added latency
empirical_basis: 0.20s approx 1.7x measured publish period (0.1151s, trial02_stamp actual_rate_hz); well under peer_timeout_s=0.5; 5% of cpa_horizon_s=4.0
expected_effect: measurable state_age increase; near-zero task-success impact expected but not assumed
contrast_against: vs A (delay-only) and vs C (delay magnitude sweep)
executable_now: NO (needs new parameterized orchestrator, design doc section 8)

scientific_purpose: probe CPA-staleness and relay-shutdown-boundary behavior under a stable large delay that should NOT by itself trip peer_timeout (corrects the retracted 0.6s claim)
empirical_basis: 2x peer_timeout_s=0.5 specifically to test the boundary; up to ~9 messages in flight (1.0s / 0.1151s period) makes the relay's non-flushing destroy_node() (network_impairment_relay.py lines 143-147) more likely to produce a tail-end gap; 25% of cpa_horizon_s=4.0
expected_effect: state_age shifted ~1.0s; possible tail-end message gap; CPA trigger timing/dcpa accuracy degraded; task completion not assumed to fail
contrast_against: vs B (delay magnitude sweep) and vs A
executable_now: NO (needs new parameterized orchestrator, design doc section 8)

jitter_distribution: uniform symmetric, range [-jitter_s/2,+jitter_s/2] added to delay_s (network_impairment.py line 45); realized release-delay range [0.0,0.30] with no clamping bias since delay_s is centered in the jitter spread
scientific_purpose: produce genuine out-of-order delivery via jitter spread exceeding inter-message spacing
empirical_basis: jitter spread 0.30s approx 2.6x measured publish period (0.1151s); centering delay_s=jitter_s/2 avoids negative-jitter clamping bias (network_impairment.py line 46: max(0.0, delay_s+jitter))
expected_effect: measurable out_of_order_count > 0 in sequence stats; wider state_age distribution than B/C; task-success impact is an open question this condition tests
contrast_against: vs A (jitter-only) and vs G (jitter component within combined)
executable_now: NO (needs new parameterized orchestrator, design doc section 8)

burst_or_dropout_params: none (independent Bernoulli only -- relay has no burst mechanism)
scientific_purpose: measure delivery-ratio degradation from moderate independent per-message loss while keeping consecutive-drop probability low enough to avoid confounding with staleness
empirical_basis: p=0.15; P(5 consecutive drops)=0.15^5 approx 7.6e-5, chosen so closing the peer_timeout_s=0.5 window (approx 4.3 publish periods) via loss alone stays rare
expected_effect: PDR approx 0.85; missing/gap counts > 0; low-probability but nonzero isolated SAFE_STOP_STALE possible; task success likely but not guaranteed
contrast_against: vs A (loss-only) and vs G (loss component within combined; matched seeds with G)
executable_now: NO (needs new parameterized orchestrator, design doc section 8)

burst_or_dropout_params: PROPOSED v1.1 extension (not built): outage_period_s (time between outage starts) and outage_duration_s (length of each full-dropout window); suggested first values to revisit once implemented: outage_duration_s=0.7 (greater than peer_timeout_s=0.5, guarantees a stale/peer-timeout event per outage by construction), outage_period_s=15.0 (approx 4-5 outages within max_runtime_s=60.0)
scientific_purpose: deterministically test STALE_STATE_STOP / PEER_TIMEOUT_STOP safety behavior via a genuine full-outage window, distinct from 'very lossy' independent-Bernoulli conditions
empirical_basis: current relay (network_impairment.py, read in full) implements ONLY independent per-message Bernoulli drop -- no burst/consecutive/periodic mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase; confirmed via full-file read and repo-wide grep for burst/consecutive-drop/outage patterns
expected_effect: designed to reliably force at least one stale/peer-timeout safety stop per outage; not approximated with an extreme independent drop_probability (would conflate 'very lossy' with 'briefly fully down' -- different failure modes)
contrast_against: vs A and vs the not-yet-run B/C/D/E
executable_now: NO -- BLOCKED on relay extension (design only, see design doc section 3)

jitter_distribution: uniform symmetric, range [-0.10,+0.10] added to delay_s=0.20 (realized range [0.10,0.30])
scientific_purpose: test whether combined moderate delay+jitter+loss produces effects beyond the sum of the individual single-factor conditions (interaction analysis)
empirical_basis: each component set at a level individually comparable to but not exceeding its single-factor condition: delay approx B's 0.20s; jitter spread 0.20s (smaller than D's 0.30s, keeping this moderate-combined rather than worst-of-both); drop_probability 0.10 (below E's 0.15)
expected_effect: combined degradation in PDR/state_age/possible reordering; whether combined > sum-of-parts (interaction) or approx additive is what this condition tests
contrast_against: vs A (full combined effect) and vs each of B, D, E individually; matched seeds with E
executable_now: NO (needs new parameterized orchestrator, design doc section 8)
